end.summary:
Practised linking bird beaks and feet to feeding and movement.
Explored how leaf and plant features suit habitats such as deserts, ponds and snowy places.
Identified plants as living because they make food using sunlight, even though they do not walk.
Described cactus spines, floating leaves and bird features; 3/4 and 4/5 unaided responses were correct in two links.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Atharv practised observing beaks, feet and leaf shapes, then connecting those features to feeding, movement and habitat. They used clear examples such as a kingfisher’s pointed beak for catching fish, duck feet for swimming, cactus spines for saving water, and broad waxy leaves for floating. Asha also revisited that plants are living because they make food using sunlight, although they do not move from place to place. At home, ask Atharv to observe one nearby plant or bird and name one feature and what it helps the plant or animal do.
